text:
sophie: quick heads-up — I'm proposing we split the onboarding pipeline into a fast sync preflight and an async deep-bench path. TL;DR: make intake non-blocking for users while still gating by thorough evaluations.

james: sounds sensible. curious how we keep compatibility checks deterministic enough when some checks are stochastic (kv-cache warms, sampling)?

liam: idea: two classes of checks. 
- sync: artifact sanity, shape/dtype, tokenizer check, tiny deterministic smoke (golden prompts).
- async: heavy latency/cost profiling, quantized runs, long eval suites with sampling.

erin: we'll also need an artifact verifier in sync to reject obviously broken exports (opset mismatch, missing weights). propose adding an `artifact-verify` step that runs `onnx.check()` + file manifest diff.

sophie: yep. sync should be short (<30s) and give clear pass/fail + intake_id. async gets an `intake_id` and runs in background, writes summaries back to registry. fallback to canary if heavybench fails.

james: how do we surface async results back to rollout? want traceability so product owners can see why a model failed gating. suggest propagate `intake_id` as trace across all bench jobs and store a compact summary plus pointer to raw logs.

liam: also bench modes: coldstart (no KV) and warmed (simulate typical workload). heavybench should do both and report p50/p95/cold-vs-warm and cost-per-token estimates.

erin: storage/cost note — raw heavybench traces are big. store compressed raw for 7 days, keep aggregated metrics (JSON summaries) forever. maybe example summary fields: `p50`, `p95`, `cost_delta_pct`, `quality_delta`.

bench-bot: enqueued 2 heavybench jobs for model m-2026-03 (intake_id=ix-9834), est runtime ~4h.

james: small UX question — what does the sync failure page look like? critical to show which step failed (artifact vs runtime-smoke) and quick remediation hints.

sophie: agree. sync response should be a concise list: failed_step, error_snippet, suggested fixes + retry link. keep human readable.

liam: gating rules suggestion: heavybench is advisory for first 24h but becomes gating after a policy phase. Also automatic rollback if quality regression > X% or cost delta > Y%. defaults: quality_drop_threshold = 5% relative, cost_increase_threshold = 10% (config per-customer).

erin: operational: add a short timeout for sync checks (30s) to avoid blocking intake, then a max TTL for async jobs (48h) and alert on unusually long runs.

sophie: action items: 1) add `artifact-verify` tool and wire to sync (owners: @james) 2) propagate `intake_id` across bench jobs and trace (owners: @james) 3) implement async queue with sample-size heuristics + cold/warm modes (owners: @liam) 4) add summary retention policy and short sync timeout (owners: @erin). I'll create GH issues. :thumbsup:

james: will do 1 & 2. quick note: include a small reproducible command for enqueuing heavybench in infra: `./intake enqueue --model m-2026-03 --mode heavy --intake-id ix-9834`

liam: will prototype sampling heuristics. question: sample size for cost estimates — maybe target 1k tokens across X prompts? we can parameterize.

erin: will add pipeline timeout and retention config. also I'll add the UI snippet for sync failure messages.

bench-bot: job 9834 finished: heavybench summary -> p50=42ms, p95=210ms, cost_delta=+8%, quality_delta=-0.2%. summary saved to registry:/models/m-2026-03/intake/ix-9834/summary.json

sophie: nice — summary looks within thresholds for default policy. keeping this split should cut median ingest latency by a lot for small models. let's reconvene after the PRs land.

james: noted. I'll open PRs today with tests for artifact-verify and intake_id propagation.

liam: ping me on the sampling heuristics thread, I'll include cold/warm combo reports.

erin: PR coming for timeouts + retention. moving to implement. :rocket:
